item.title: Megacity particulate matter airsheds redefine urban pollution exposure boundary
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04192-6

Megacity particulate matter airsheds frequently extend far beyond administrative boundaries, highlighting the need for cross-jurisdictional pollution management, according to analyses of population exposure for 53 global megacities.
item.dc:title: Megacity particulate matter airsheds redefine urban pollution exposure boundary

item.title: Radioactive fallout legacy of nuclear tests in soils of the Southern Hemisphere
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04218-z

Distinct radionuclide patterns in understudied Southern Hemisphere regions can be predicted using machine learning-based random forest models that integrate spatial uncertainty into cesium and plutonium baseline inventory maps.
item.dc:title: Radioactive fallout legacy of nuclear tests in soils of the Southern Hemisphere

item.title: The first filling of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD): hydrological and operational insights
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04201-8

Exceptionally wet years and effective mitigation measures largely buffer the downstream impacts of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam’s first filling, while unilateral implementation without data exchange exacerbates mistrust among riparian states. Publicly available data and an integrated modelling proved effective in transboundary water management.
item.dc:title: The first filling of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD): hydrological and operational insights

item.title: Late Quaternary drainage reorganization of the Sutlej River system at the Himalaya mountain-foreland transition
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04204-5

Sutlej River occupied a west and a south-flowing strand with the drainage reorganization occurring through river bifurcation and avulsion between <60 and 15 ka through a tectonically controlled process, as shown using optically stimulated luminescence geochronology and sedimentary, structural and geomorphic analysis.
item.dc:title: Late Quaternary drainage reorganization of the Sutlej River system at the Himalaya mountain-foreland transition

item.title: Rapid transient uplift driven by active slab tear, southern Calabria, Italy
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04207-2

Marine terrace sediments in southern Calabria, Italy, yield a mean burial age of 118.8 ± 8.7 ka across a broad elevation range, indicating uplift rates of up to 12 mm yr⁻¹ that are likely driven by active tearing of the subducted Ionian slab and resulting buoyancy-driven isostatic rebound.
item.dc:title: Rapid transient uplift driven by active slab tear, southern Calabria, Italy
